findings.text: blocking: importing reckon.env_duration before ensure_interpreter at line 106 defeats the stdlib-only bootstrap path; a bare hook under a Python without reckon installed fails before it can re-execute in the checkout interpreter.

follow-on: the expected default is taken from the same production constant passed by each getter to read_duration_override, so changing that constant moves both sides together and does not guard the plan's no-default-changes requirement; the same weakness occurs at lines 99-101.

item_verdicts.done_when: §31 requires parser and site-bound tests, a census, base/head importer gates and a bound-removal control; the manifest names ten migrated sites and the recorded gate logs show base 78 passed, head 98 passed, and control 13 failed.

justifications.durability: tests/test_a_duration_override_is_read_one_way.py:29 fails for wrong fallback or rejected valid values, :34 fails if exclusive zero is accepted, :94 fails when site bounds are removed as the control confirms, and :99-104 fails for inverted lease or grace zero rules, but :94 and :99-101 cannot detect a changed production default.
justifications.evidence: the source run's base-gate-resumed.log and head-gate-resumed.log finish with EXIT=0 and 78/98 passing cases, while negative-control.log ends EXIT=1 with 13 failing cases when the lower-bound check is removed.
justifications.fit: reckon/env_duration.py:7 follows the compact helper idiom and introduces no forbidden name, but reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:98 breaks the hook's bootstrap-first import ordering.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/env_duration.py:7 implements the required bounds for the migrated getters, but reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:98 can prevent a bare hook from reaching its interpreter bootstrap.
justifications.reuse: the capability search found reckon/crew/session_host.py:154 parsing an injected mapping with a different seam, so reckon/env_duration.py:7 supplies the process-environment reader without duplicating that owner.
